attacks.claim: Retrieval is moved to a Vector Store provisioned outside the EU, so customer chunks and embeddings, which the agreed DPA constraint says must be processed and stored in the EU, would be stored in the US when tenants cut over in week 4.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap." No fallback or EU-only alternative is stated.

attacks.claim: The agreed constraint makes the 4,100-case regression suite the release gate for any model change, but the plan defers it to week 6+ so the week 4 cutover of all tenants happens without it.
attacks.evidence: "the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover."

attacks.claim: In week 3 the plan deletes the fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters and releases the A100 reservation before the week 4 cutover. If the cutover fails or Atlas-L regresses, there are no weights or GPUs to restore service.
attacks.evidence: "release the A100 reservation ... and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage" (Week 3), followed by "Week 4: cut all tenants over to Nimbus".

attacks.claim: Sequencing error: tenants stay on vLLM until the week 4 cutover, but the GPU reservation is released in week 3. Production inference for every tenant would have no serving capacity during that window.
attacks.evidence: Week 3: "release the A100 reservation"; Week 4: "cut all tenants over to Nimbus (generation + retrieval)"; no interim capacity is mentioned.

attacks.claim: Week 5 removes pgvector, vLLM manifests, and the GPU node pool from Terraform before any full regression run, which removes the rollback path while quality is still unverified.
attacks.evidence: Week 5: "remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform." Week 6+: "regression suite run, prompt tuning on any failures."

attacks.claim: The parity conclusion rests on 25 hand-picked questions judged by two lawyers, with no statistical test and no long-context cases, yet the plan uses it to waive the regression gate and claims Atlas-L is better at up to 200k context, which was never tested.
attacks.evidence: "ran 25 representative questions ... Atlas-L was preferred in 19 of 25 and tied in 3. This confirms quality parity or better"

attacks.claim: Practice-area behaviour currently encoded in LoRA adapters is replaced by system prompts drafted in week 1, and their equivalence is validated only after cutover. Behaviour changes for every practice area could ship unverified.
attacks.evidence: "practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts (drafted in week 1 by the applied team)."

attacks.claim: Zero data retention is documented only for generation on the org account. Vector Store, which holds chunk text and vectors, and embed-3 have no stated retention terms, so customer-derived data could be retained by the vendor.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)" is listed under Generation only; Vector Store and embeddings have no retention statement.

attacks.claim: The region for the embed-3 endpoint is not stated, although ingest workers send customer document chunks to it. Those embeddings are DPA-covered derived data that must stay in the EU.
attacks.evidence: "Embeddings: Nimbus embed-3 (1,536 dims), called from the ingest workers." No region given.

attacks.claim: Moving customer documents and prompts to a new third-party processor (Nimbus) likely requires sub-processor notification or consent under the existing DPAs and client confidentiality terms for law firms. The plan does not address this.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no sub-processor notice, customer notification, or DPA amendment step in the plan's timeline or risks.

attacks.claim: The projected Nimbus generation cost of $7,900/mo, which drives the claimed $8,990/mo saving, has no token-volume or pricing basis. With the GPUs already released, a cost overrun cannot be reversed.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus generation (est.) | $0 | $7,900"; no token volume, pricing source, or budget math is given.

attacks.claim: Generation and retrieval become a single external dependency with no stated timeouts, retries, circuit breaker, fallback, SLA, or alerting, and the self-hosted fallback is deleted in week 3. A Nimbus outage would take down the whole product.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no fallback, SLA, retry/timeout policy, or observability; Week 3 deletes the GPU reservation and weights.

attacks.claim: The exit cost is high and the plan deletes the exit path. Weights and adapters are deleted, pgvector is removed, and retrieval moves to a proprietary managed store with no export or self-host option stated.
attacks.evidence: "delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters"; "drop pgvector and its index-maintenance jobs"; no export or self-hosting path is described.

attacks.claim: Headroom is about 3x on request rate, and no token-per-minute quota is stated, even though 200k-context requests multiply token load. A 3x traffic increase could hit limits, although this is a projection rather than a current failure.
attacks.evidence: "our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s."

attacks.claim: Per-tenant API key issuance, storage, and rotation are not specified. Only a single 30-day rotation policy is stated, and it is unclear whether it applies to tenant-scoped keys.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus API keys live in Vault ... rotated every 30 days"; "tenant-scoped API key" with no lifecycle detail.

attacks.claim: The latency comparison (640 ms vs 910 ms) does not state matched prompt lengths or whether it covers long-context requests, so the improvement is not shown to hold for the workloads that matter.
attacks.evidence: "Atlas-L p95 time-to-first-token measured at 640 ms from our Frankfurt pods (1,000 requests, week of 10-05), vs 910 ms on vLLM."

attacks.claim: Re-embedding about 41M chunks and dual-writing in a single week with 3 engineers has no throughput or rate-limit math, so the week 2 feasibility is unproven.
attacks.evidence: "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."
